summary: DIRECTER proposes a plausibility-guided decoding loop that dynamically modulates KV-cache steering strength per decoding step, combined with a one-time attention-sensitivity layer ranking, to mitigate oversteering in activation steering for instruction following. The method is well-motivated, clearly described, and evaluated across three benchmarks, five models (1B-14B, two families), with meaningful ablations (fixed-strength, reversed/random ranking, random tokens) and efficiency analysis. The main weaknesses are the absence of error bars or significance testing on the main results, a limited set of steering baselines (only PASTA and SpotLight), and a somewhat heuristic top-1-token plausibility criterion. Overall this is a solid, useful contribution slightly above the typical borderline ICLR submission.
strengths: Well-motivated problem (oversteering in static activation steering) with an elegant, training-free solution: accept/reject steering per step via a plausibility check against the raw distribution, with progressive halving of steered layers.

The gating mechanism (skipping steering when the raw top-2 probability already falls below beta * top-1) is provably correct and keeps overhead modest (~16% throughput, negligible memory), making the method practically deployable.

Broad empirical coverage for this subfield: IFEval, LIFBench, and a new GSM8K-Format benchmark; generalization across Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Qwen-2.5 3B/7B/14B; plus text-quality/task-fidelity evaluation with both an LLM judge and corroborating human evaluation.

Good ablation and robustness suite: fixed-strength variants (ST1-ST6) isolate the value of dynamic control; reversed ranking, random layers, and random tokens validate the sensitivity ranking and instruction-span targeting; robustness to beta, alpha (over orders of magnitude), and prompt format is shown.
The plausibility filter is shown to transfer as a safety gate to other steering methods (Figure 2b), supporting the claim of a general anti-oversteering mechanism.

key_concerns.issue: No error bars, seed variance, or significance tests on the main results (Tables 1, 2, 4). Gains over tuned baselines (e.g., 76.5 vs 72.1 avg; IFEval P.Acc 78.8 vs 76.5) are on benchmarks with only hundreds of prompts, so some margins may be within noise. Only the random-layer/token ablations report +/- values, showing the authors can measure variance but chose not to for headline numbers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report variance across multiple prompt shuffles/seeds (or bootstrap CIs over prompts) for Table 1 and Table 2, and add a paired significance test for the key comparisons vs SpotLight-tuned and zero-shot.

key_concerns.issue: Only two steering baselines (PASTA, SpotLight) are compared. The activation-steering literature is larger (contrastive activation addition / representation-engineering-style vector methods, ITI-style head interventions, and other inference-time control methods), and the claim of 'surpassing prior steering methods by ~4%' rests on this narrow set.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one residual-stream steering-vector baseline (e.g., CAA/RepE-style) and ideally one additional recent attention-level method, or explicitly scope the superiority claim to attention-level instruction-following steering.

key_concerns.issue: The plausibility criterion uses only the top-1 token of the steered distribution (Eq. 1). This is a weak proxy for distributional plausibility; alternatives (top-k overlap, KL/JSD thresholds) are not explored in the main text.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ablate the plausibility measure (top-k acceptance, KL threshold) or justify why top-1 suffices; at minimum discuss this design choice.

key_concerns.issue: Baseline hyperparameters are tuned on IFEval and then applied to other benchmarks, which risks mild test-set selection bias favoring IFEval-tuned baselines on that benchmark while DIRECTER uses untuned fixed settings; the asymmetry is actually conservative for the authors but the tuning protocol should be clearer.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Clarify the tuning protocol (validation split vs. test set) and, if possible, tune baselines on a held-out split of IFEval.

key_concerns.issue: Task fidelity and text quality rely primarily on gpt-4o-mini as judge, a relatively weak evaluator; human evaluation is relegated to the appendix with no detail in the main text on annotator count, agreement, or sample size.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Summarize the human evaluation protocol (n annotators, n samples, inter-annotator agreement) in the main text and consider a stronger judge model for the headline Table 4.

key_concerns.issue: No evaluation of general capability side-effects (e.g., MMLU-style benchmarks) beyond instruction-following tasks; the 'no trade-off' claim is supported only by text quality and task fidelity on the evaluated distributions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a small general-capability check or scope the no-degradation claim to the evaluated settings.

questions_for_authors: How many prompts/examples underlie each number in Table 1, and what is the bootstrap confidence interval for the 6.5% average improvement and the ~4% margin over tuned steering baselines?
Why is plausibility defined only via the top-1 token (Eq. 1)? Did you try distribution-level criteria (top-k overlap, KL divergence), and how sensitive is the method to this choice?

The sensitivity analysis steers one layer at a time and averages disturbance scores (Eq. 2-3): does the ranking interact with the choice of alpha used during profiling, and is the ranking stable across prompts within a task (i.e., could it be computed once per model rather than per prompt)?

For the gating mechanism: what fraction of decoding steps are skipped in practice, and how does the 16% throughput overhead decompose between the one-time ranking, skipped steps, and rejected steering attempts?
Does DIRECTER compose with sampling-based decoding (temperature > 0)? All experiments use greedy decoding; does the plausibility check behave sensibly when the raw distribution is flat?
How was the human evaluation in Appendix E.3 conducted (number of annotators, samples, agreement), and did annotators see paired outputs blind to condition?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well-scoped: the 6.5% average gain matches Table 1, limitations (heuristic sensitivity metric, separable instruction-span assumption) are explicitly stated, and 'significantly' is used loosely given the absence of significance testing, which is the main calibration gap.

significance.justification: Oversteering is a recognized practical problem in activation steering, and a modular, low-overhead fix that also improves other methods would be used and cited by the controllable-generation community.

novelty.justification: Per-step accept/reject of steering via plausibility against the raw distribution, plus sensitivity-ranked progressive layer removal, is a genuinely new combination, though it borrows ideas from speculative/contrastive decoding and KV-quantization sensitivity analysis.

rigor.justification: The method is sound, the gating argument is correct, and the ablation design isolates each component; the top-1 plausibility heuristic and lack of theory for the sensitivity metric are acknowledged limitations.

statistical_soundness.justification: Greedy single-run results with no error bars or significance tests on any main table, despite modest benchmark sizes and margins of a few points; only the random ablations report variance.

calibration_honesty.justification: A real limitations section, conservative fixed hyperparameters, and honest reporting of cases where steering baselines fail; minor overreach in 'significantly enhances' and generality phrasing without statistical backing.

clarity.justification: Well-organized with a clear algorithm, intuitive figure captions, and readable prose; Eq. 2 is dense and some phrasing is awkward, but the method is understandable end-to-end.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (intro, related work, method with preliminaries, RQ-driven experiments, analyses, conclusion with limitations) at appropriate length.

reproducibility.justification: Fixed hyperparameters (alpha=100, beta=0.5, greedy decoding), named public benchmarks and models, algorithm pseudocode, and appendix pointers for prompts and tuning details make reproduction feasible.

related_work.justification: Fair and specific positioning against PASTA and SpotLight with concrete cost comparisons, but the steering-baseline coverage is narrow and residual-stream steering methods are discussed only in prose, not empirically.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting displays: method overview, fixed-strength and compatibility ablations, beta/alpha/prompt robustness, and efficiency trade-offs; Table 5's qualitative example directly illustrates the failure mode fixed.

breadth_generality.justification: Three benchmarks, five models across two families and 1B-14B scale, and good ablations, but only two steering baselines and no general-capability evaluation limit support for the broadest generality claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a well-executed, useful inference-time method whose acceptance hinges on adding variance/significance reporting and broadening the steering-baseline comparison.
